We begin by identifying resonance. The differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+36{\pi }^{2}y=f(x)
$$

has a natural frequency of 

$$
\omega =\sqrt{36{\pi }^{2}}=6\pi .
$$

The frequencies of the forcing harmonics for a $1$-periodic function $(L=\frac{1}{2})$ are 

$$
{\omega }_{n}=\frac{n\pi }{(\frac{1}{2})}=2n\pi .
$$

For $n=3$, we have ${\omega }_{3}=6\pi .$ Since ${\omega }_{3}=\omega ,$ the $n=3$ harmonic of the forcing function causes resonance.

For the $n=3$ harmonic, the forcing term is 

$$
{f}_{3}(x)=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x).
$$

Because this frequency matches the natural frequency, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{3}}=x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x)).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{{p}_{3}}^{′} & =(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x))+x(-6\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x)+6\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)) \\ {y}_{{p}_{3}}^{″} & =-12\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x)+12\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)-36{\pi }^{2}x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x))\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{{p}_{3}}^{″}$ and ${y}_{{p}_{3}}$ into the equation ${y}^{″}+36{\pi }^{2}y=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x):$

$$
[-12\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x)+12\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)-36{\pi }^{2}{y}_{{p}_{3}}]+36{\pi }^{2}{y}_{{p}_{3}}=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)
$$

The resonant terms involving $x$ cancel out, leaving

$$
-12\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x)+12\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x)=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi x).
$$

Now, equating the sine and cosine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-12\pi A=0 \\ 12\pi B=\frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}A=0 \\ B=\frac{1}{108\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resonant component of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{{p}_{3}}=\frac{x}{108\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi x).
$$
